hypothesis: Iter 82 = realistic per-patient BASELINE DIVERSITY in the teacher, the confirmed root cause of the iter-81 gate failures (glucose_mape 0.49 > 0.20, hr_mape 0.18 > 0.15; big recovery from iter-80's 1.45 but still failing). iter-81 added the per-patient glucose baseline mechanism (b_emb) but the trained model's achievable fasting glucose still floored at ~88 mg/dL and resting HR at ~68 bpm, because the teacher's patient population was clinically too narrow (randomize_params Gb sigma=0.15 ~ 82-110, HR0 sigma=0.15 ~ 60-81): the per-patient mechanisms only learned authority over the trained range. The benchmark eval is a per-patient flat-baseline test spanning glucose 60-118, hr 49-77, sbp 94-133, dbp 61-88 (uniform staircases; persistence scores ~0.009-0.01), so the under-sampled LOW baselines stayed unrepresentable and the model lost to persistence. FIX: widen the teacher baseline spreads to clinically realistic ranges — Gb 0.15->0.25 (~59-171 mg/dL +/-2sigma), HR0 0.15->0.22 (~46-111 bpm), SBP0 0.10->0.14 (~91-158), DBP0 0.10->0.15 (~59-108). HR/SBP/DBP are learned-dynamics with no hardcoded anchor, so a wider training range alone should unlock their low ends; glucose's b_emb mechanism (iter-81) now has training signal across the full range to learn its authority. Teacher verified physiologically SANE across the widened range (40 sampled patients, Gb [59,171], HR0 [46,111], 0/40 unstable trajectories). NOT reverting the Ra amplitude term (iter-80): meal glucose appearance is correct physics; the eval window is fasting so Ra is silent there — flattening predictions by removing real physics would degrade the SYSTEM to game the benchmark. This iter changes ONLY the teacher patient diversity (randomize_params); model architecture + recipe (params) unchanged from iter-81, so the benchmark is attributable to exactly the baseline-diversity widening.
expectedEffect: PRIMARY (the iter-81 gate failures): (1) glucose_mape drops below 0.20 — with the teacher demanding fasting baselines down to ~59, b_emb learns authority to calibrate the benchmark's low users (60-87) instead of flooring at 88; correct per-patient baseline on a fasting eval approaches persistence (~0.009). (2) hr_mape drops below 0.15 — the learned CV dynamics, trained on resting HR down to ~46, can now represent the benchmark's low-HR users (49-67) instead of flooring at ~68. (3) overall_weighted_mape recovers toward iter-79's ~0.08; skill_vs_persistence turns less negative across markers. SECONDARY: sbp/dbp (negative skill -4/-9, same flat-baseline gap) improve as their baselines now cover the benchmark lows. WATCH: per-user — the previously-floored LOW users (glucose 60-87, hr 49-67) should improve most; mid-range should hold (iter-81 already handled them). RISKS: (R1) wider patient dispersion means fewer samples near the population center per epoch — the cohort/trajectory signals still cover it, but if mid-range regresses, the spread is too aggressive (back off Gb to ~0.20). (R2) extreme patients (Gb 171, HR 111) are rarer/harder; if they add noise without benchmark benefit, cap the spread. (R3) temp is NOT addressed (benchmark temp is flat 37 for all users — its negative skill is the model over-predicting temp excursions, a separate fix, not a baseline-range gap).
